prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals

- Climate and investment
  - A £400bn National Transformation Fund (including a £250bn Green Transformation Fund) and a National Investment Bank with Regional Development Banks to lend £250bn over 10 years.
  - OBR to factor climate impacts; listing rules to delist firms that don’t contribute to climate goals.
  - Targets by 2030: ~90% low‑carbon electricity and 50% low‑carbon heat; 7,000 offshore and 2,000 onshore turbines; major solar rollout; trial tidal and expand hydrogen; new nuclear; permanent fracking ban.
  - Retrofit almost all 27m homes to high efficiency; expand heat pumps, district heat and storage; grid upgrades.
  - Windfall tax on oil; public ownership of energy networks and supply arms; public ownership of water.

- Transport and infrastructure
  - Public ownership of rail; full electrification; HS2 to Scotland; Crossrail for the North; reopen local lines; expand rail freight.
  - Councils empowered to run/regulate buses; restore 3,000 routes; free bus travel for under‑25s where councils control services.
  - More cycling/walking investment; end new ICE car sales by 2030; national EV charging; transition public fleets to zero‑emission; taxi/private hire reforms.

- Industry, skills and work
  - R&D to 3% of GDP by 2030; support for steel and foundation industries; three gigafactories; plastics remanufacturing; climate‑focused procurement.
  - Reform Apprenticeship Levy; Climate Apprenticeships with targeted bursaries.
  - Real Living Wage of at least £10 for 16+; end zero‑hours contracts; single “worker” status; rights from day one; sectoral collective bargaining; flexible working; extend parental leave; ban unpaid internships; new workplace rights enforcement body; aim to reduce average full‑time week to 32 hours within a decade with no loss of pay.

- Public services
  - Presumption to insource; take back PFI over time; public sector pay restored with year‑one 5% rise; 20:1 public‑sector pay ratio cap.
  - £150bn Social Transformation Fund for schools, hospitals, care homes and housing.

- Health and care
  - Average 4.3% annual health funding uplift; end competitive tendering; capital plan; more scanners; data safeguards.
  - Abolish prescription charges in England; free annual NHS dental check‑ups; free hospital parking; net‑zero NHS.
  - Expand GP training; boost mental health (24/7 crisis care; modernise facilities; children’s hubs and counsellors).
  - National Care Service with free personal care for older people; lifetime cap on costs; improve care workforce pay and conditions.

- Education
  - Expanded early years (Sure Start Plus; 30 hours free for all 2–4s; extend for 1s); 150k extra staff; graduate‑led workforce.
  - Class size cap of 30 in primary; scrap SATs; Arts Pupil Premium; bring academies/free schools under local oversight.
  - Lifelong learning entitlements (to Level 3 and six years at Levels 4–6); restore ESOL; abolish tuition fees and restore maintenance grants.

- Social security and disability
  - Replace Universal Credit; immediate mitigations: end five‑week wait and sanctions; scrap benefit cap and two‑child limit; raise Local Housing Allowance; split payments; multi‑channel access.
  - End outsourced disability assessments; improve ESA and Carer’s Allowance; support for independent living.

- Housing and homelessness
  - Build 1m+ social homes over a decade; at least 150k/yr by end of term (100k council social rent); zero‑carbon homes standard.
  - End Right to Buy for social housing; new land powers; “use it or lose it” for stalled sites.
  - Rent controls linked to inflation with local powers; open‑ended tenancies; end Section 21; national landlord licensing; renters’ unions.
  - £1bn fire safety fund; remove dangerous cladding; end rough sleeping within five years with 8,000 homes and expanded services.

- Policing, justice and rights
  - Rebuild neighbourhood policing (officers, PCSOs, staff); minimum standards for victims.
  - Presumption against prison sentences under six months for non‑violent/non‑sexual offences; reunify probation; restore legal aid.
  - Measures on violence against women and girls (commissioner, refuge funding, no‑fault divorce, decriminalise abortion).

- Digital, culture, sport, gambling
  - Free nationwide full‑fibre broadband by 2030 via a public provider; online duty of care; Charter of Digital Rights.
  - £1bn Cultural Capital Fund; protect free museum entry; media plurality and governance reforms.
  - Football governance reforms (supporter representation, safe standing); new Gambling Act with limits, levy and ad curbs in sport.

- Local government and communities
  - Restore council spending power over the parliament; insource local services; Post Bank; high‑street measures; library standards; National Youth Service.

- Migration and asylum
  - End hostile environment and indefinite detention; close named detention centres; safe legal routes; right to work for refugees; automatic rights for EU nationals; protect family reunion.

- Constitution and elections
  - Abolish House of Lords and replace with an elected chamber after a constitutional convention; votes at 16; voting rights for all residents; automatic registration; repeal Fixed‑term Parliaments Act; stronger lobbying and transparency rules; restrict second jobs.

- Devolution, Brexit, international and defence
  - Increased investment for devolved nations.
  - Renegotiate a deal (customs union, close single‑market alignment, rights protections, EU agencies/security) and hold a referendum on that deal vs remain; safeguard NI arrangements; guarantee citizens’ rights.
  - Human‑rights‑led foreign policy; War Powers Act; increase diplomatic capacity; suspend specified arms exports linked to violations; climate diplomacy; recognise Palestine.
  - Maintain NATO and 2% GDP defence; renew deterrent; defence industrial strategy; veteran support; green targets for defence estate.
